items.headline: US outages across NSA, FAA, Microsoft 365 and Apple draw official 'not an attack' statements; causes cited are maintenance, updates and legacy kit
items.summary: NSA's classified internal network (NSANet) was disrupted on 17 November during maintenance. It followed Microsoft 365, FAA and Apple outages. Officials told Congress on 18 November they found no sign of cyber attack; FAA and Microsoft have published technical causes, NSA has not.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: The NSA, FAA, Apple and Microsoft each acknowledged their own disruption, and the FAA and Microsoft gave technical causes. The 'no cyber attack' finding is a statement by US officials (DNI, DHS, FBI) and company statements, not an independently published investigation.

sections.happened:
NSA's classified internal network, NSANet, was disrupted on Tuesday 17 November at Fort Meade. The agency called it 'temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance' and said mission-critical capabilities stayed operational. The Record, citing sources, said staff arrivals were staggered, non-essential staff received a 'Code Gray' notice, and disruption continued into 18 November, with full restoration possibly taking another day or two.

It followed a Microsoft 365 outage (12–13 Nov), an FAA nationwide ground stop (13 Nov), JPMorgan Chase and Zelle problems, a United Airlines outage, and Apple service outages on 17 Nov that Apple attributed to an internal update.
sections.technical:
NSA has published no technical cause. DNI Jay Clayton said the outage was maintenance affecting PHP; a source told The Record that was correct. Whether the vulnerability was AI- or human-derived is unknown.

FAA (Q&A page): legacy equipment destabilised when data flooded its FTI network at about 1,000 connection attempts every 4–5 seconds; 17 of 22 en route centres were affected. Suspected origins were a radar site in Amarillo, Texas and a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where L3Harris was deploying a new Juniper router.

Microsoft (preliminary report, via BleepingComputer): a July gateway-server bug, a Teams failover traffic surge and about 14% capacity already offline left over 80% of gateway servers unresponsive.
sections.guidance: No fixes or workarounds apply to NSANet. FAA says it disabled the originating Juniper routers' functionality, disabled it on over 60 others, paused installations and will reevaluate maintenance timing. Microsoft says it added capacity, monitoring and safeguards, with a final report due. DHS Secretary Mullin said a call with private-sector representatives would discuss notifying customers before upgrades.
sections.differing: Clayton, Mullin and FBI Deputy Director Raia told the House Homeland Security Committee they have seen no indication of a coordinated or foreign attack; Mullin said he was 98 percent confident. Earlier, Mullin said AI may have been responsible. Schumer called the timing 'too coincidental' and urged a red team review, reporting by 1 December.
sections.unknown: NSA's root cause beyond 'maintenance' and PHP, the restoration date, and whether any data was affected are unpublished. FAA and L3Harris root cause, Microsoft's final report, and any link between incidents remain open.

items.headline: Suspected Chinese APT rebuilds EggStreme malware to target Philippine government
items.summary: Bitdefender's November 2026 update says a suspected Chinese APT rebuilt parts of the EggStreme framework after its 2025 exposure, still targeting Philippine government bodies; Taiwan targeting is low-to-medium confidence.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Vendor research; victims not named; no independent confirmation found.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (UK time not stated), Bitdefender blog update; Infosecurity Magazine and The Hacker News same day

sections.happened: Bitdefender published an update to its September 2025 EggStreme research on 18 November 2026. It says a suspected Chinese APT rebuilt parts of the framework after exposure, possibly triggered by its report. It assesses with high confidence that Philippine government organisations, with multiple victims, remain targeted. Taiwan is a lead at low to medium confidence.
sections.technical: DLL sideloading, file-share lateral movement, in-memory execution and mutual TLS persist. Changes: new config protection, RC4 to RC5 then custom loader cipher, raw TCP agent protocol, passive listener builds, and no keylogger in newer agents. No CVEs cited.
sections.guidance: Bitdefender recommends restricting unneeded built-in Windows tools, detecting DLL sideloading by library name and location, finding unmanaged machines that reach workstations, and watching for new inbound listeners.
sections.differing: Palo Alto Networks tracks CL-STA-1048, which used EggStremeFuel and Loader from March to September 2025. Bitdefender says this is consistent with its observations but has not compared infrastructure or victims, so the link is unconfirmed.
sections.unknown: Initial access vector is unknown. Bitdefender could not determine how the logon script or valid credentials were obtained. Victim identities and Taiwan targeting remain unconfirmed.

items.headline: European Commission confirms cyber campaign disrupted HR systems for about 10 days
items.summary: The European Commission confirmed a detected cyber campaign that disrupted HR systems for about 10 days. Officials say most of the attack is contained; whether staff personal data was accessed is unconfirmed.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Commission spokesperson confirmed a detected cyber campaign; data exposure unconfirmed.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, c.11:30 UK time (Politico report, relayed by Reuters/JPost)

sections.happened: Politico reported on 19 November 2026 that the European Commission was hit by a cyberattack lasting about 10 days, which may have compromised personal data. Sysper, MyPMO (medical reimbursements) and translation services were disrupted. Spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed a detected cyber campaign. The Commission's top crisis body met; Henna Virkkunen briefed commissioners on 18 November.
sections.technical: Reported as an AI-assisted campaign. Techzine and Cybersecuritynews, citing Politico, name the publicly available AI tool ARTEX used to find IT vulnerabilities; the spokesperson did not name a tool. No CVEs, IOCs, ATT&CK mapping or attacker attribution published. CERT-EU and the EDPS were informed.
sections.differing: Politico-based reports say the campaign ran about 10 days; Alarabiya says it occurred in October. The spokesperson said no evidence yet of a breach affecting staff as a whole; Euronews says data exposure is still being assessed.
sections.unknown: Whether staff data was accessed or exfiltrated, attacker identity, initial access vector, and full scope remain unknown. JSIS remained unavailable per Euronews.

items.headline: Rakuten Securities test-environment breach may expose up to 15.72 million accounts
items.summary: Japanese brokerage Rakuten Securities says customer data in a test environment may have leaked externally. About 4.47 million accounts had personal and financial details; passwords and PINs were not confirmed exposed.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Company published apology and notice; figures are company-stated ceilings, leak unconfirmed.
items.firstReported: Nov 17 2026 (UK time not stated in sources; company notice published 17 Nov, Japan time), via Rakuten Securities notice, reported by Infosecurity Magazine and Japan Times

sections.happened: Rakuten Securities, a Tokyo-based online broker, detected possible unauthorised access on 16 November and cut access. Its investigation found information in a test environment may have leaked externally on 11 November. It announced this on 17 November. Up to 4.47m accounts had personal and financial details; up to 11.25m had only branch/customer codes and login IDs.
sections.technical: Production customer data was present in a test environment, which normally uses dummy data. The company has not disclosed the attack vector, attacker, or cause; the investigation is ongoing. No CVE or ATT&CK mapping has been published.
sections.guidance: Rakuten Securities urges customers to switch to passkey (FIDO2) login, reports over 90% already use it, warns of phishing, and says its emails contain no links.
sections.differing: Reports sum the tiers to 15.72m; the company says there is no overlap and that 15.72m is a maximum including former customers. One blog says the tiers overlap, which the company's spokesperson account contradicts.
sections.unknown: Cause, attacker, entry method and why production data was in test are unknown. Whether data left the network is unconfirmed. Regulator notification is not reported.

items.headline: TfL takes Oyster photocard website offline after compromise; about 265,000 customers' account details may be exposed
items.summary: TfL says around 265,000 Oyster photocard customers may have had account details (names, contact details, dates of birth, security answers) compromised. Passwords and payment data are said to be unaffected. The site is offline; the ICO has been notified.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: TfL (Shashi Verma, director of technology strategy and revenue) acknowledged the incident, the 265,000 figure and the data categories in statements carried by BBC, The Register, Infosecurity Magazine and others; the TfL portal notice is also quoted. TfL's own pages could not be fetched directly.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (BBC and Telegraph reports, evening UK time); The Register and Infosecurity Magazine followed on 19 Nov (Register 11:01 UK)

sections.happened: Transport for London says it became aware on Monday 16 November 2026 that Oyster photocard customers were receiving emails asking them to create accounts they already held. TfL said the emails came from its own systems but were generated as a result of the compromise. It took the photocard website offline and later said around 265,000 customers may have had account details compromised. Card types: Zip Oyster, 18+ Student, 18–25 Care Leaver, 60+ London, Apprentice and Veterans. TfL says the incident is contained and affected customers have been contacted, with ianVisits reporting this began on Wednesday 18 November. The ICO is notified. Existing cards still work; renewals go through customer services. The site was still offline on 19 November.
sections.technical: TfL has not disclosed the entry method, actor, tooling or any IOCs, and no CVE or ATT&CK mapping has been published. Per TfL, data that may have been accessed: names, email and home addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, and security questions and answers. TfL's current assessment is that passwords, bank or payment card details, journey information, and names and dates of birth of children with Zip Oyster cards were not compromised; ianVisits also reports TfL said photo copies were not leaked. The unsolicited account-creation emails were sent from TfL's own systems, which TfL linked to the compromise. TfL says there is no evidence yet that the data has been misused.
sections.guidance: TfL says it will ask all photocard customers to change their password, security question and answer, and says customers who reuse the same details on other services should change them there. TfL states existing photocards remain valid at ticket barriers, and customer services handles renewals and journey-history queries while the site is offline.
sections.differing: No competing accounts. Wording varies: BBC reports details were "accessed" after "suspicious activity"; TfL says details "may have" been compromised. The Register's headline refers to compromised customer accounts, while TfL's quoted statements refer to account details. The Register notes nothing currently suggests a link to the September 2024 incident.
sections.unknown: The intrusion method and timing, whether the 265,000 figure will change, the attackers' identity, whether data has been copied or sold, and when the website will return.

items.headline: Microsoft's official agent-framework PyPI package published with credential stealer in versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2
items.summary: Two malicious releases of Microsoft's agent-framework (about 190,000 downloads a month) were uploaded to PyPI on 17 November and quarantined within an hour. A Python startup hook harvested Azure, CI/CD and developer credentials. How the attacker obtained publishing access is not established.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: A Microsoft spokesperson told The Register it had made some repositories private 'while we investigate malicious content' (the statement does not name the package). PyPI quarantined both versions, and StepSecurity, Wiz, Aikido, OX, Socket and others independently analysed the wheels and reported the same payload, file names and exfiltration URL. No Microsoft advisory or post-incident write-up was found.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (UK time = UTC): 1.26.1 uploaded 20:35; vendor write-ups from that evening (Socket 23:05); press from 18 Nov (BleepingComputer, SecurityWeek, The Register, The Hacker News), Help Net Security 19 Nov

sections.happened: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's `agent-framework` meta-package on PyPI carried a credential stealer. Per StepSecurity's registry timestamps (UTC, same as UK time in November), 1.26.1 was uploaded at 20:35:20 on 17 November and quarantined at 21:06:16. Version 1.26.2 followed at 21:08:39 and was quarantined at 21:16:44. Wiz reported both gone from PyPI by 21:30. The last clean release is 1.26.0 (12 November). The package has about 192,534 monthly downloads (OX) or about 41,000 weekly (Wiz); how many installs were of the malicious versions has not been published. Microsoft told The Register it had made some repositories private while investigating malicious content.
sections.technical: Both wheels add a `.pth` file that runs at every Python start, without importing the package: `agent_framework_meta.pth` with `_telemetry.py` (1.26.1), `af_runtime_diag.pth` with `af_runtime_diag.py` (1.26.2). They keep the genuine `agent-framework-core==1.26.0` dependency. The payload harvests matching environment variables, up to 300 other processes' `/proc` environments, and credential files (Azure CLI, pip, npm, Git, Docker, Hugging Face, `.env`). It requests Azure managed-identity and Azure DevOps OIDC tokens; 1.26.2 adds GitHub Actions OIDC. Data is zlib/base64-encoded and POSTed to `webhook.site/d381fd80-ec62-42ad-8f5c-d1b15103c9bb`. Wheel SHA-256 for 1.26.1: `d27fa344…e110`; 1.26.2: `3d20a8bc…e0a9`. No CVE assigned; no actor attributed. Likely ATT&CK (brief's mapping): T1195.002, T1552.001, T1552.005, T1528, T1567.
sections.guidance: StepSecurity, Wiz, OX and Aikido advise isolating affected hosts before running Python or pip, rebuilding from a clean base pinned to 1.26.0, rotating reachable credentials, and searching egress logs for the webhook UUID path. StepSecurity notes rotation does not revoke already-issued identity tokens. No Microsoft advisory was found; PyPI lists 1.26.0 as latest.
sections.differing: Entry vector is disputed. The Register's standfirst suggests a compromised GitHub org admin account. StepSecurity says evidence does not establish the vector or account, though its flow chart mentions a newly added maintainer account; PyPI lists two maintainers. OX suggests the wheel-build flow was hijacked; Aikido's metadata analysis points to a hand-edited wheel uploaded with valid credentials.
sections.unknown: How the attacker obtained publishing rights, their identity, and whether access was revoked are unknown. Install counts, credentials actually exfiltrated and tokens actually issued are unpublished; StepSecurity says static analysis shows attempts only. Microsoft has given no root cause.

items.headline: Critical Apache Roller RCE CVE-2026-129448 under active exploitation
items.summary: Apache says unauthenticated deserialization flaw CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 9.8) in Roller XML-RPC is being actively exploited. Exploitation details and victims not disclosed.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: ASF advisory reported by several outlets; advisory itself not read
items.firstReported: Advisory dated 17 Nov 2026 (Apache, per SecurityWeek); first press report 18 Nov 2026 05:35 per BleepingComputer (time zone not stated). UK time not confirmed.

sections.happened: The Apache Software Foundation said CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 9.8) in Apache Roller is being actively exploited. Versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 are affected. It is the same flaw as CVE-2026-82384, which was fixed in September 2026 and listed only 6.1.5. Apache has not described attacks, attackers or victim counts.
sections.technical: Unsafe deserialization in the XML-RPC endpoint: vendor extension types are deserialized before the requester authenticates, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Disabling XML-RPC in the admin UI does not prevent it. Credited to researcher n0mi1k; reported by Matt Raible. No MITRE ATT&CK mapping published.
sections.guidance: Apache recommends upgrading to Roller 6.1.6 or later. Where that is not possible, Apache describes setting enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or removing the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping, then restarting Roller.
sections.differing: Press reports state the flaw was fixed in 6.1.6; SecurityWeek adds that 6.1.7 (11 Nov) addresses 15 further flaws. No conflicting accounts of the facts found.
sections.unknown: Exploitation methods, threat actor, number of compromised servers and targets are not disclosed. No IOCs published. Whether CISA has listed it is not confirmed.

items.headline: Java4Shell: critical OpenJDK Base64 flaw (CVE-2026-114938) patched; exploitation probing under way
items.summary: Calif disclosed CVE-2026-114938, a heap overflow in OpenJDK's AVX-512 Base64 decoder, on 17 Nov; Oracle and OpenJDK shipped fixes and CISA issued an alert. Sensor operators report probing from 17-19 Nov, with no confirmed compromise.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Oracle and OpenJDK published fixes, CISA, Canada and Switzerland issued alerts, Cisco/Red Hat/Elastic/Atlassian published advisories; probing is reported independently by GreyNoise, Previdian, watchTowr and Cloudflare. Successful in-the-wild compromise is not confirmed.

sections.happened: Calif disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder, on 17 November 2026. The Hacker News reported Calif saying the flaw had leaked before disclosure. OpenJDK and Oracle released fixed builds at 13:00 PT (21:00 UK); Calif's write-up followed, and CISA issued an alert that evening. Calif demonstrated unauthenticated RCE on Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, and authenticated RCE on Kafka, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit and Spinnaker. From 17 to 19 November GreyNoise, Previdian, watchTowr and Cloudflare reported probing; none reported confirmed intrusions. Cisco, Siemens, Elastic, Red Hat, Atlassian, Keycloak and Jenkins have published advisories; several fixes are still pending.
sections.technical: Heap buffer overflow (CWE-122) in HotSpot's x86-64 Base64 intrinsic using AVX-512 VBMI. Per Calif, padded tail input underflows the output length, the store mask becomes all ones, and 64 bytes are written to a 50-byte buffer. Trigger: 64 'A' characters plus '='. Preconditions: OpenJDK 17.0.6 or later (17, 21, 25, 27); Intel Ice Lake onward or AMD Zen 4 onward; ARM unaffected. Oracle scores CVSS 3.1 8.1; Calif 4.0 9.2. RCE needs heap grooming, a heap leak and a per-application chain. Calif's PoC only triggers corruption; VulnCheck says a full exploit is available to its customers. Observed probes used 'java4shell-recon' User-Agents; Cloudflare saw one IP use both Artex and Java4Shell. No ATT&CK IDs published; vector resembles T1190.
sections.guidance: Oracle fixed builds, per Canada's Cyber Centre: 8u513-perf, 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1. Calif, Talos and Canada list -XX:UseAVX=2; Calif also lists -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics. CISA lists Base64 input validation and size limits. Cisco lists no workarounds; Atlassian cites disabling AVX-512 for Data Center. Keycloak 26.8.2-3 images carry a patched runtime.
sections.differing: Oracle rates it 8.1 (High complexity); Calif and Talos 9.2. Calif says chains were built with AI assistance; VulnCheck and watchTowr call RCE hardware- and application-specific and expect no indiscriminate exploitation. OX Security's headline estimates under 0.12% of JVMs at RCE risk (page unread). Early reports predicted only a crash; 18 November 'no exploitation' statements were superseded by sensor data.
sections.unknown: Whether any probing led to compromise. Origin of the pre-disclosure leak. Fix dates for Cisco, Siemens, Elastic and Atlassian Data Center. Whether Calif publishes its withheld product exploit chains. Previdian lists the CVE as not in CISA KEV.

items.headline: PHP schedules critical security release for 19 November; PHP2Shell flaws already exploited
items.summary: PHP announced security releases for all supported versions on 19 November (14:00–14:30 UTC), top severity CRITICAL, in non-default or uncommon setups. CVE-2026-115560, an RCE vector, is expected. Details unpublished. The October PHP2Shell flaws are under exploitation, including on PAN-OS and Check Point gateways.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: PHP's own php.net notice (18 Nov) confirms the release window and CRITICAL ceiling but names no CVEs, versions or scores; CVE-2026-115560 is tied to the release only by PHP's 23 Oct statement and outlet reporting. Exploitation of the earlier PHP2Shell flaws is separately confirmed (CISA KEV, Palo Alto, Check Point).

sections.happened: PHP's security team announced on 18 November that security releases for all supported PHP versions are scheduled for Thursday 19 November, 14:00–14:30 UTC (same as GMT in the UK). It said the highest severity is CRITICAL, that critical issues need non-default configuration or uncommon setups, and that details and fixed versions will come with the releases. php.net listed no release entry at the time of research. Outlets link the release to CVE-2026-115560, an RCE vector in session upload progress that PHP described on 23 October; the 18 November notice names no CVEs. It follows the 21 October PHP2Shell fixes (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619), since exploited, including against PAN-OS and Check Point gateways.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-115560 (CVSS and affected versions unpublished) needs session.serialize_handler set to php_binary or php_serialize, code switching it to php with ini_set() before session_start(), and session upload progress enabled (the default). PHP2Shell: CVE-2026-109618 (out-of-memory handling leaves request data uninitialised) and CVE-2026-109619 (stale request state after memory is freed); both CVSS v4.0 9.2, unauthenticated, fixed in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35. Palo Alto reported exploitation of exposed PAN-OS management interfaces (T1190). Dream reported chaining with kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 to root 25 systems. Check Point Research reported attacks from 30 October on Mobile Access portals: privilege escalation via CVE-2026-123039, web shells, TSGA/TSProxy backdoor, destroy_v6 wiper on ESXi.
sections.guidance: PHP (23 Oct): set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular release and restart workers; applications never switching the serialize handler at runtime can keep it enabled. PHP (18 Nov): details and fixed versions will accompany the releases. PHP2Shell fixes: 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35. Palo Alto: patched customers are not affected. CISA added both PHP2Shell CVEs to KEV on 26 October.
sections.differing: PHP Foundation (to The Register, October): CVE-2026-115560 needs a very unlikely combination, not expected in practice. A GitHub repository describes a proof of concept on php:8.4.27-apache; not independently run. PHP2Shell scores vary: PHP 9.2 (CVSS 4.0), Fortinet 9.8 (v3), Palo Alto 8.7 then 9.2. Check Point says attribution is uncertain; ESET linked the malware family to China-nexus UNC5221.
sections.unknown: CVE list, affected and fixed versions and scores for the 19 November release were unpublished. That CVE-2026-115560 is the critical issue is inferred. No exploitation of the new flaws is reported. Number of affected deployments is unknown.

items.headline: Ukraine and FBI arrest four ransomware group members tied to $40.5M in ransoms
items.summary: Ukrainian police, working with the FBI, detained four key suspects of a ransomware group that police say took over $40.5M from at least 28 companies.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Police acknowledged arrests and figures; reported by two outlets; primary statement second-hand.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026, c.18:08 (timezone unstated), BleepingComputer; Help Net Security followed 19 Nov 2026

sections.happened: Ukrainian police, working with the FBI, detained four key suspects of an international ransomware group after a two-year investigation. Police say at least 28 companies paid over $40.5M in ransoms. Authorities ran 66 searches in Kyiv and 11 regions. Suspects are charged with participation in a criminal organisation and unauthorised interference with information systems.
sections.technical: Attackers impersonated IT support by phone, using a platform with AI-generated voice messages, to obtain credentials or get remote-access software installed. Court records describe phishing pages mimicking corporate VPNs, spoofed numbers, and TeamViewer or AnyDesk. Court records name Chaos as the ransomware used. Data was stolen before encryption.
sections.differing: Reporting links members to former Conti members and BlackSuit; Ukrainian authorities have not confirmed individual affiliations with Conti or BlackSuit.
sections.unknown: Full extent of damage is still being established. Arrest locations are undisclosed. Further members are being identified.

items.headline: France attributes fridge cyberattack to Iran
items.summary: Schneier on Security reports US intelligence reached a 'low confidence' assessment that Iran was behind attacks in France. The French attribution and CERT report were not read.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Anonymous US officials via one blog; French CERT report not accessed.
items.firstReported: 18 November 2026, 7:05 AM UK time (approx.; Schneier on Security post, US time not stated), first source Schneier on Security

sections.happened: On 18 November 2026 Schneier on Security reported that U.S. intelligence agencies recently reached a 'low confidence' assessment that Iran was responsible for attacks in France, citing three anonymous U.S. officials. Iran was also seen as probably responsible for similar attacks elsewhere in Europe; those probes are early-stage.
sections.technical: Reported as involving internet-exposed device interfaces, tagged 'Internet of Things' and 'infrastructure' by the blog. No ATT&CK IDs, CVEs or IOCs were read. The French CERT report CERTFR-2026-CTI-009 was not accessible.
sections.differing: The US assessment is 'low confidence' and names Iran generally, not a specific group. Reader comments claim a French CERT report cites Farsi code strings; this is unverified and false-flag is raised.
sections.unknown: The French government's own attribution statement, CERT report content, victims, scale and vendor response are unverified.

sources.title: Schneier on Security: France Is Blaming Iran for the Fridge Cyberattack (blog, citing anonymous US officials)

items.headline: Nvidia halts H200 sales to China as US tightens chip export rules
items.summary: Nvidia said it is no longer shipping licensed H200 data-center chips to China, as Washington tightened export reviews and remote-access limits. Tencent's president said the clampdown 'sets everyone back'.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Nvidia earnings-call remarks as reported by secondary outlets; transcript not read.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026, 22:33 UK time (Semafor, 5:33pm EST); earnings call 17 Nov US time

sections.happened: On its Q3 FY2027 earnings call (17 Nov, US time), Nvidia said it is no longer shipping licensed Hopper data-center products to China and excluded China Hopper sales from Q4 guidance. Washington tightened export reviews on 16 Nov.
sections.unknown: Nvidia gave no official reason for the halt. Reports say about 600,000 H200s are held in Hong Kong, and Beijing has withheld approval for large imports.
sections.differing: Kress says the backlog means revenue is unaffected; Jefferies estimates a $44–62bn cut to next-year data-center revenue.

items.headline: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share, raising about $81.3B, largest on record
items.summary: Anthropic priced its Nasdaq IPO at $83 a share, above the $70–$78 range, selling 980M shares for about $81.3B; trading set for 19 November.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Company press release; multiple outlets report same figures.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026, US evening (approx. 23:00–00:00 UK) via Anthropic press release and Reuters pre-pricing reports

sections.happened: Anthropic, PBC priced its IPO of Class A common stock at $83.00 per share on 18 November 2026, selling 980,000,000 shares (956,351,354 by the company). Shares are set to trade on Nasdaq as ANT on 19 November. Reported proceeds are about $81.3B, the largest IPO on record, above SpaceX's June offering.
sections.differing: Valuation: about $1.5T on a fully diluted basis (CNBC, TechCrunch, AP); Globe and Mail reports about $1.1T non-diluted. Figures are consistent across outlets otherwise.
sections.unknown: First-day trading price and closing outcome; whether the 30-day underwriter option of 147M shares is exercised.
